build: CHRONOLOGY: never return a separate ordering; sequence is always []. Where a passage states the order of two events explicitly (a date, 'after', 'then', 'before', 'while'), state that order inside the claim about the later event, in the passage's own terms; never infer order from paragraph order, thematic logic, a comparison, or an interpretation treated as an event. Each claim asserts ONE consequential action or proposition; do not bundle events from different times into one claim; choose the strongest eight rather than compressing a whole history into compound claims. Preserve location, direction of movement, quantifiers, modality and rhetorical questions: reaching a destination is not entering its surrounding city; a possible action is not an action taken. unknowns name details of the CASE the passages cannot establish (dialogue, sensory detail, motives, numbers, the order of events); an unknown never discusses which author or document the passages come from, whether they match the proposed episode, or what the proposed source would have said, because provenance is recorded as metadata and corrected by review.
review: Try to falsify each claim: could its cited passage be true while part of this claim is false? If yes, reject that claim and identify the unsupported step. Check exact action, location, direction of movement, quantifiers, modality, rhetorical questions and bundled events, not just shared names. A claim stating temporal order (before, after, then, a date) is supported only if its passage states that order explicitly; order inferred from paragraph order, thematic logic, a comparison, or an interpretation treated as an event is unsupported. Check every qualifier in canonicalEpisode, including its title: retain no unsupported period boundary, scope or cultural classification. A descriptive title may shed an unsupported qualifier while preserving the supported case; this never permits replacing a particular missing record with a biography or an unrelated event. Judge unknowns against the canonicalEpisode you return, not the provisional episode: an unknown about which author or document the passages come from, or whether they match the proposed episode, is provenance rather than an unknown and makes unknowns inaccurate; so does an unknown denying something an accepted claim establishes.
